dct_description_sm: Upper right margin: H42.; Title in map.; Text below image in Latin and German.; Relief shown pictorially.; Plan view of Poreč showing the fortified town and the Benedictine monastery on St. Nicolas' Island in the foreground. Includes a lion attacking a goat in the foreground representing Venetian domination over Istria with a Latin phrase advising patience in the face of oppression--edited dealer description.; "Meisner's 'emblem book' containing over 800 pictorial-poetic compositions, was enormously popular throughout Europe in the 17th century. The plan views were based on the work of De Bry, Braun & Hogenberg, Merian and others with the addition of emblematic figures or scenes in the foreground, juxtaposed with moralizing and edifying verses veneath the image and a Latin motto at top. It was originally issued with 52 plates as the 'Thesaurus philo-politicus in 1623-24... the plates then appeared in the eight parts of 'Sciographia Cosmica' published by Paulus Furst between 1637-78. The plates for these editions were renumbered alphanumerically in the upper right corners- A-H (identifying the 8 parts) and 1-100 (plate number). They were finally issued in 1700 and 1704 in Rudolf J. Helmer's 'Politica-politica.'"--Dealer description.; Probably separated from Meissner's Sciographia Cosmica.
1 view 7 x 15 cm on sheet 15 x 19 cm
